tools.name: browser_open
tools.description: Open a URL in the session's browser and return the loaded page.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element by CSS selector (Playwright selector syntax).

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type text — into `selector`'s field when given, else the focused element.

tools.name: browser_read
tools.description: Read the current page: url, title and visible text.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page by a pixel delta (negative = up).

tools.name: browser_eval
tools.description: Evaluate JavaScript in the page and return the JSON value.

tools.name: terminal_run
tools.description: Run a shell command in the session's terminal and return its output + exit code.

tools.name: terminal_write
tools.description: Send raw input to the terminal (interactive programs; use terminal_run for commands).

tools.name: terminal_read
tools.description: Read the terminal's recent output (scrollback tail).

tools.name: workbench_previews
tools.description: List dev-server preview URLs the user's Workbench shows for this session (URL scan + PREVIEW: markers).

tools.name: workbench_open
tools.description: Show the user something in this session's Workbench: `{file, line?}`, `{diff, path?}`, `{pr}`, `{url}` or `{tab:'subagents'|'background'|'plan'}` — the panel opens on that tab. A session with no folder accepts `tab` targets only (the rest error). It never opens an editor on the Mac.

diff.description: Open the Changes tab — the session's live git diff

pr.description: Open the PR tab for the thread's pull requests

url.description: Preview URL to open on the Preview tab

tab.description: Engine tab to open (the only kind a folderless session accepts)

tools.name: context
tools.description: Who and where this session is: the employee record, channel, thread, folder, context usage { used, window }, the user's name, Mac status and attached tool areas.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: LilOS docs shipped with the app — pass a topic (overview, threads, employees, approvals, workbench, mobile, gateway); none returns the index.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask the user and wait. Optional why, ifYes and ifNo are the lines Needs you shows. With options, the user picks one; without them, they approve or deny.

tools.name: team_list
tools.description: The company roster: every employee's name, role, status, model, and who they report to.

tools.name: thread_post
tools.description: Post a message to this session's own thread — the user sees it in the app.

tools.name: thread_read
tools.description: Read the visible messages of one of your threads — the session's own unless `thread` names another by id or title; `before`/`afterSeq` window it.

tools.name: thread_list
tools.description: Your threads — title, state, last activity and linked PRs.

tools.name: thread_search
tools.description: Search messages across your threads (the relay's FTS index).

tools.name: thread_set_title
tools.description: Rename this session's thread — only while its title is auto-generated; a user-typed title wins and returns `user_title`.

tools.name: thread_prs
tools.description: Pull requests linked to this session's thread.

tools.name: thread_start
tools.description: Ask the user to start a new thread with `text` as its first message (optional `title`; optional `project` — an id or key from project_list — whose folder it works in, else a plain chat). Waits for approval; company changes always ask.

tools.name: team_hire
tools.description: Ask the user to hire an employee (name, role, model, instructions; `profile` reuses an existing engine profile). Waits for approval; returns the new employee record. Every agent may propose a hire, and a company with no CEO still can.

tools.name: team_set_ceo
tools.description: Ask the user to give the CEO position to an employee. Everyone who reported to the previous CEO or to the owner then reports to them; they report to the owner. Waits for approval.

tools.name: team_update
tools.description: Ask the user to update your own employee record — name, role, model, instructions, or who you report to. Never edits another employee. Waits for approval.

tools.name: folder_add
tools.description: Ask the user to add a folder to the recent-folders list so it can be picked for a session. Waits for approval.

tools.name: project_list
tools.description: The company's projects — name, key, folder, about. Pass a project's id or key to thread_start.

tools.name: project_create
tools.description: Ask the user to make a project of a folder (optional name, about). A folder that already has a project answers it. Waits for approval; returns the project record.

tools.name: goal_list
tools.description: The company's goals — title, project, due, why.

tools.name: goal_create
tools.description: Propose a goal (project id or key, title, optional due and why). Always asks before it is written. Returns the goal.

tools.name: ticket_list
tools.description: The company's tickets. Optional project (id or key) limits the list.

tools.name: ticket_read
tools.description: One ticket: status, owner, what it waits on, checklist, result, updates.

tools.name: ticket_create
tools.description: Create a ticket in a project (id or key). Does not ask. An owner is recorded; assigning them is ticket_assign, which opens their thread.

tools.name: ticket_update
tools.description: Change a ticket's title, status, waiting-on, checklist, or result. Does not ask and does not change the owner. Returns every ticket the write moved, including one that was waiting on a ticket you just finished.

tools.name: ticket_assign
tools.description: Give a ticket to one employee (ownerId, or "ceo" for whoever stands in). Handing a ticket to an agent is the CEO's job: only the holder's session is offered this, and with no CEO it is offered to nobody. Does not ask. Sets the owner and opens their thread in one step. Assigning again adds the next hand's thread.

tools.name: ticket_comment
tools.description: Add an update on a ticket, as yourself. Does not ask.

tools.name: update_post
tools.description: Post a short note on Home and in Inbox. kind is plan, finished, handed, stuck, or note. Does not ask. Only the CEO's session is offered this, and with no CEO it is offered to nobody.

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.description: This employee's scheduled tasks — name, schedule, access level, last run.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a scheduled task for yourself — name, schedule, prompt, optional folder. Asks the user to approve.

tools.name: schedule_update
tools.description: Edit one of your scheduled tasks — only the fields given change; folder: null clears it. Asks the user to approve.

tools.name: schedule_delete
tools.description: Delete one of your scheduled tasks — its future runs stop. Asks the user to approve.

tools.name: schedule_run_now
tools.description: Fire one of your scheduled tasks now — a session opens at once. Asks the user to approve.

tools.name: task_create
tools.description: Hand a job to another LilOS employee (`agent` = name or id from team_list). The task runs as a visible child thread with only your prompt — the child never sees this thread's history, and its access is yours, never broader. Does not ask. In a git repo the child gets its own worktree from your current commit by default (isolation "shared" works in this thread's folder instead); your uncommitted changes are never copied and merging back stays a separate step. The child's finish wakes this thread with the result inlined (task_read has the rest); `requestId` makes a retry return the same task.

tools.name: task_read
tools.description: Check one of your tasks — status, its child thread id, and the delivered result. Only children this thread created are visible; a task id another thread created is not found.

tools.name: task_wait
tools.description: Wait for one of your tasks to finish — returns the task's latest state, or `timedOut` when `timeoutMs` hit with it still running (a timeout never cancels the child).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Cancel one of your running tasks — interrupts the child thread's turn and never wakes this thread. An already-finished or cancelled task just returns its state.

tools.name: coding_agents
tools.description: The user's stored default model + effort for each outside coding agent (claude, cursor, devin, antigravity). A missing agent or field means that CLI's own default — pass flags only for stored values.

tools.name: coding_agents_set
tools.description: Ask the user to change the stored default model and/or effort for one coding agent (`null` clears a field back to the CLI default). Waits for approval; returns the updated defaults.
